definitions.explanation: Thin, soft paper used for wiping or cleaning.

examples.english: To blow your nose with tissue paper.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{塵紙|ちりがみ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{配|くば}っていた→配る：03921_kubaru⟧。
examples.english: They were handing out tissue packets in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {塵紙|ちりがみ}⟦{交換|こうかん}→交換：02746_koukan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{来|き}た→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.notes: Referring to trucks that exchange old newspapers for tissue paper.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{塵|ちり}→塵：12107_chiri⟧ (dust) + ⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧ (paper). A somewhat old-fashioned word for tissue paper. In modern Japanese, ⟦ティッシュ→ティッシュ：08816_tisshu⟧ is far more common in everyday speech.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ティッシュペーパー→ティッシュペーパー：23909_tisshupeepaa⟧: tissue paper (most common today)
- トイレットペーパー: toilet paper

CULTURAL NOTE:
- {塵紙|ちりがみ}⟦{交換|こうかん}→交換：02746_koukan⟧: a once-common service where trucks drove through neighborhoods collecting old ⟦{新聞|しんぶん}→新聞：01440_shinbun⟧ and exchanging them for tissue paper
- In Japan, ⟦ポケット→ポケット：02964_poketto⟧ tissues are often handed out free at ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧ as ⟦{広告|こうこく}→広告：02747_koukoku⟧ — a unique Japanese custom

The word {塵紙|ちりがみ} is still understood but sounds dated to younger speakers.
